flags.text: The bank trap notes use capitalized emphasis (UP, LARGER, ADD) and the multiplication glyph; the notes here are plain case and ASCII.

routing: Works today: the anchor scrolls the QR engine to this skill section, with its pattern card, its picture and its worked examples. A first-visit tour opens on top (Skip closes it), and the section header reads LOCKED until its prerequisites are marked mastered, though everything in it still shows. The page also carries a timed simulator, a streak counter and mastery counts in its other views; the anchor lands on the section, not on those.

every served choice (5) has a note; one key

served.stem: Compute (5 × 10⁻⁶)(7 × 10⁵) and give the answer in proper scientific notation.
served.bankWhy: 5 × 7 = 35 and 10⁻⁶ × 10⁵ = 10⁻¹. 35 × 10⁻¹ is not proper form, so write 3.5 × 10⁰. Answer: 3.5 × 10⁰.

answer.line: Fronts multiply to 35, powers add to 10^-1, and 35 x 10^-1 in proper form is 3.5 x 10^0.

steps: Split the job. Multiply the front numbers: 5 x 7 = 35.
Add the exponents: -6 + 5 = -1. So far, 35 x 10^-1.
Fix the front. 35 = 3.5 x 10^1, so the front gets ten times smaller and the exponent grows by 1: 3.5 x 10^0.

choices.note: 5 + 7 = 12 adds the front numbers. In a product the fronts multiply: 5 x 7 = 35.
Turning 35 into 3.5 makes the front ten times smaller, so the exponent must rise by 1. Stopping at 10^-1 makes the number 10 times too small.
A smaller front number needs a larger power of ten. Moving the exponent from -1 down to -2 shrinks the number a second time.
-6 x 5 = -30 multiplies the exponents. When powers of ten multiply, their exponents add: -6 + 5 = -1.
35 x 10^-1, with the front put between 1 and 10.

student.lockIt: Multiply the fronts, add the exponents, then slide the front between 1 and 10.

playWith.label: Exponent Laws: pick multiply, set the base and both powers, and watch the exponents add

video.title: Scientific notation: fronts multiply, powers add

rows.move: front divided by 10, exponent up by 1

exits.label: Multiply the exponents instead and you get 10^-30.
Write 3.5 x 10^-1 here and the number is 10 times too small.

visual.alt: Worked lines: the fronts 5 x 7 = 35, the exponents -6 + 5 = -1, together 35 times ten to the -1, then 3.5 times ten to the 0, outlined as the answer. Two dashed side notes show multiplying the exponents and stopping at ten to the -1.
visual.caption: Look at the last arrow: the front is divided by 10 while the exponent climbs by 1, so the value never changes.
